title: AtomMem: Learnable Dynamic Agentic Memory with Atomic Memory Operation
reason: 核心贡献是让智能体学习何时用摘要和 CRUD 操作保留或修订外部记忆。两类基准上报告了相对静态及可学习基线的平均增益；摘要未给出消融效应量或适用边界。
abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents increasingly face tasks that require reasoning over extremely long range. A key bottleneck is memory design: most prior approaches treat memory as a static, human-designed component, limiting adaptability. Inspired by biological memory evolution, we propose AtomMem, a framework that exposes a set of atomic memory operations—including summarization and CRUD primitives—as tool-like actions. The agent learns a policy over these operations purely via reinforcement learning, using only the task reward. AtomMem allows the agent to dynamically interleave summarization and CRUD to retain important information while managing memory efficiently. We evaluate AtomMem on streaming long-context understanding and web-navigation benchmarks, demonstrating an average improvement of 8.5 points over static memory workflows and 2.1 points over the current learnable-memory baseline. Ablation studies show that both summarization and CRUD are essential to train agent memory. The project can be accessed at https://github.com/RUCBM/AtomMem.
